[chunk 3/5] MATERIAL FINDINGS:

1. ACQUISITION ACTIVITY & INTANGIBLE ASSET CONCENTRATION
   - IBM acquired HashiCorp (Q1 2025) and StreamSets/webMethods (7/1/2024 from Software AG)
   - Intangible asset balance grew $1.593B in H1 2025, primarily from acquisitions ($2.329B added)
   - Goodwill additions in Software segment: $4.994B (H1 2025), up from $1.511B (FY 2024)
   - Future amortization obligation: $13.9B over remaining life (est. $1.4B in remainder 2025, $2.6B in 2026)
   - Client relationships intangible: $6.148B (up from $5.317B at 12/31/2024)
   - RISK SIGNAL: Rapid acquisition pace with heavy goodwill/intangibles loading; impairment risk if synergies underdeliver

2. FINANCING RECEIVABLES SECURITIZATION
   - 26-month revolving agreement (effective 1/1/2025) to sell up to $1.3B of short-term commercial financing receivables
   - H1 2025: $3.715B transferred (vs $3.686B in H1 2024); $686M uncollected at period end
   - These qualified as "true sales" and were derecognized from balance sheet
   - Net loss on transfers: $25M (H1 2025) vs $33M (H1 2024)
   - RISK SIGNAL: Off-balance-sheet financing receivable transfers; true-sale treatment masks underlying credit exposure

3. DEBT PORTFOLIO EXPANSION
   - Short-term debt: $8.945B (6/30/2025) vs $5.089B (12/31/2024) — 76% increase
   - Long-term debt: $64.164B (6/30/2025) vs $54.943B (12/31/2024) — 17% increase
   - Finance lease obligations: $1.180B (6/30/2025) vs $1.000B (12/31/2024) — 18% increase
   - New issuances (2/10/2025): $3.6B Euro notes + $4.75B USD notes
   - Pre-swap obligations: $65.242B (up from $56.112B)
   - RISK SIGNAL: Rapid debt accumulation coinciding with M&A activity; leverage expanding

4. RECEIVABLES CREDIT QUALITY DETERIORATION
   - Client financing receivables: $11.357B (6/30/2025) vs $10.418B (12/31/2024)
   - Non-investment grade (Ba1–C): $2.258B (19.9% of portfolio) vs prior $2.172B (20.9%)
   - Amortized cost not accruing: $90M (6/30/2025) vs $97M (12/31/2024)
   - Allowance for credit losses: $136M (6/30/2025) vs $123M (12/31/2024)
   - Write-offs H1 2025: $14M vs $3M in FY 2024
   - RISK SIGNAL: Credit losses increasing; receivables portfolio aging and diversifying geographically

5. CASH FLOW HEDGE VOLATILITY
   - Unrealized losses on cash flow hedges (FX and interest rate): $(419)M (6/30/2025) vs $121M (12/31/2024)
   - Foreign exchange derivative notional: $10.7B for royalty/cost hedges; $5.9B for FX-denominated debt
   - Net investment hedges notional: $7.5B (6/30/2025) vs $6.2B (12/31/2024)
   - Estimated reclassification from AOCI to NI: $(442)M within next 12 months
   - RISK SIGNAL: Significant FX hedge losses deferred in AOCI; potential P&L volatility if rates move further

6. OPERATING LEASE PROGRAM
   - Gross profit on sales-type/direct financing leases: $765M (H1 2025)
   - Interest income on lease receivables: $115M (H1 2025)
   - Total lease income: $930M (H1 2025) vs $596M (H1 2024) — 56% increase
   - Note: Carrying value excludes unguaranteed residual value (RVG risk embedded)
   - RISK SIGNAL: Operating lease program expanding; residual value guarantee exposure not quantified

7. CONTINGENT LIABILITIES & LITIGATION
   - IBM Pension Plan litigation (joint/survivor annuity benefits): Remanded to district court 4/3/2025 for discovery
   - Brazil tax challenges: ~$350M potential exposure (company disputes materiality)
   - Environmental (CERCLA/Superfund): Multiple ongoing remediation obligations
   - IP/patent litigation: Material exposure undisclosed (company cites complexity of estimation)
   - RISK SIGNAL: Pension plan litigation reopened; tax contingencies in Brazil; IP litigation opaque

8. RELATED-PARTY FINANCING
   - IBM International Capital Pte. Ltd (IIC): 100% owned finance subsidiary of IBM
   - IIC issued $5.5B of U.S. dollar notes (Q1 2024) in tranches 2–30yr maturity, coupons 4.6–5.3%
   - IIC notes fully and unconditionally guaranteed by IBM
   - Purpose: Borrow money for benefit of IBM and affiliates
   - RISK SIGNAL: Captive finance subsidiary structure; debt guaranteed by parent; used to fund M&A/operations

9. STOCK-BASED COMPENSATION & ACQUISITIONS
   - H1 2025 stock-based comp: $492M (net) vs $414M (H1 2024) — 19% increase
   - Unrecognized comp cost: $2.5B (as of 6/30/2025) to vest over 2.4 years
   - Assumption of HashiCorp stock-based awards in Q1 2025 acquisition
   - RISK SIGNAL: Dilution from equity compensation and assumed awards in acquisitions
